name: Serve cached Bright Data web search and page reads to Claude and Cursor over MCP

parameters.content:
## Give Claude or Cursor web access without giving them your key

Point any MCP client at this workflow and it gains six web tools backed by Bright Data: Google search, Google's AI Overview with the pages it cites, People Also Ask, Bing search, Bing news, and a page reader that returns markdown.

### How it works
The MCP Server Trigger publishes one bearer-gated endpoint. Each tool re-enters this same workflow through the Execute Workflow Trigger, so every call passes a gate before it reaches Bright Data.

The gate is the point. An MCP client is a loop: ask Claude one question and it may search three times, read two pages, then search again to check itself. Repeats are served from a cache in the workflow's static data, and the day's calls are counted against a budget you set, so a runaway agent cannot spend the whole scraping balance overnight. Every answer tells the model how many calls it has left.

Responses are repaired before the model sees them. Bright Data answers a wrong zone with HTTP 200 and an error body, which reads as "nothing found" - here it comes back as a sentence saying what to fix. Base64 images, screen-reader text and Google redirect wrappers are stripped: a measured Google response was 105KB, about 94% of it image data no model can see.

### Setup
Add your Bright Data API key as a Header Auth credential (`Authorization` / `Bearer YOUR_KEY`) and attach it to the four HTTP Request nodes. Put a Bearer Auth credential on the MCP Server Trigger and give the same token to your client. Set your zone names, your daily budget and your cache lifetime in the Limits node.

## 1. The endpoint and its six tools
One bearer-gated MCP URL. Every tool calls this same workflow back through the trigger in section 2, which is what lets a call be cached, capped or refused.

## 2. The gate
Every tool call lands here. A cached answer or a refusal goes straight back without spending a request; anything else is routed to the search it needs.

## 3. Bright Data
Three of the tools share one Google response - organic results, the AI Overview and People Also Ask all arrive in the same payload. Bing web search is the slow one, around 40 seconds.

## 4. Shape, cache, return
Errors that arrive as HTTP 200 become readable sentences, base64 images are stripped, the answer is cached, and the reply says how many calls are left today.

## 5. Try it before wiring Claude
Optional. An agent pointed at this same server, so the tools can be tested in the Chat panel first. The endpoint is localhost - change it if your n8n runs elsewhere.

## Set these two before the first call

Zones default to `serp_api1` and `web_unlocker1`. If yours are named anything else, change them in Limits or every call fails.

The cache and the counter live in workflow static data, which n8n only saves on production executions. A run started from the canvas always reports a miss. Activate the workflow and call it over MCP.

options.systemMessage:
You answer questions using the web tools on the connected MCP server, and you
only state things those tools returned.

Pick the tool that fits: search_web for general questions, search_bing for a
second opinion or to see what grounds Copilot, search_news for anything recent,
google_ai_overview when the question is what Google itself answers, and
related_questions when you are exploring a topic rather than looking something
up. Search results are titles and snippets, so when the answer depends on detail
rather than on which pages exist, call read_page on the most promising link.

Every response carries calls_left_today. When it gets low, stop searching and
answer from what you have. A response with ok:false carries an error sentence -
read it and act on it rather than repeating the same call.

Cite the URL you took each fact from. If the tools return nothing useful, say so
rather than filling the gap from memory.
